edges.rationale: Trubetzkoy did not merely coin a convenient label for an area others had already delineated (the coining-exclusion pattern this order names, and the pattern this corpus already declined an edge for entirely in Whewell/uniformitarianism) -- his 1929 paper is credited with defining morphophonology's object of study for the first time, and his 1939 book gave it its first systematic treatment. That is founding/formalizing a subdiscipline, which the coining exclusion does not reach.

What would refute this: live sources framing the 1929 paper as merely naming alternations Baudouin de Courtenay and others had already described piecemeal, with no distinct definitional act of Trubetzkoy's own -- collapsing this into the coining-exclusion pattern after all -- or fewer than two independent sources using explicit founder-grade language at this specific grain. This is the strongest, most specific claim in this batch, but it rests entirely on my own unverified recollection of the 1929 paper's existence and role, which I could not fetch this session.

Also grounded in foundry/held.json's blocking_condition on person:nikolai-trubetzkoy, which I read directly and which names Baudouin de Courtenay as 'a prior claimant' at the morphophonology grain, without specifying what relation grade the underlying source used -- I am not copying a grade from that record, since it does not state one.

edges.rationale: Baudouin de Courtenay's 1890s work is, as far as I can honestly reconstruct, standardly treated as the forerunner Trubetzkoy built on and explicitly named -- not as an independent, competing act of founding the same named subdiscipline himself: he neither used the term nor, on my own recollection, delineated it as a distinct field of study the way Trubetzkoy's 1929 paper did. That is the textbook shape of `influenced`, unlike the subfield:microbiology precedent (Pasteur/Koch, with the live Leeuwenhoek gap) where multiple figures each independently claimed founder-grade credit for the same specific content.

What would refute or change this: if live sources instead credit Baudouin de Courtenay with founding-grade language for morphophonology specifically (not just the general phoneme concept), rivaling Trubetzkoy's -- QC should upgrade this to `founded_or_formalized` alongside Trubetzkoy under the record-not-resolve plural-founder norm already established for subfield:microbiology. person:baudouin-de-courtenay -> founded_or_formalized -> subfield:historical-linguistics (order candidate 5) resolved as NO EDGE and NO NODE-JUSTIFYING claim on this target. Historical-comparative linguistics as a field was established by the early-19th-century generation (Rasmus Rask 1814, Jacob Grimm 1822, Franz Bopp) and consolidated by the Neogrammarians (Brugmann, Osthoff, Leskien) from the 1870s -- decades before Baudouin de Courtenay's own active period (Kazan School, 1870s-1890s) and well before his 1929 death. A founder's contribution cannot postdate the founding of the thing it supposedly founds, so founded_or_formalized to the field itself is unavailable to him regardless of how significant his other work was -- this is the same referent-predates-the-claimant problem this corpus's own precedent already excluded Whewell/uniformitarianism on, not the separate coining-exclusion. His own best-attested, most distinctive contribution (the phoneme concept, the phonetic/psychophonetic alternation distinction) is synchronic/structural, not historical-comparative; to the extent he engaged historical linguistics at all it was as a critic pushing back against strict Neogrammarian sound-law regularity by incorporating psychological and analogical factors -- a critique/refinement of an existing paradigm, not a founding act. I cannot honestly name a narrower subfield grain (e.g. an internal-reconstruction or sound-change-theory node) where founder-grade sourcing for him might actually sit, because no such node exists in /data for me to check and I have no live source this session to propose one from -- declining entirely rather than guessing a narrower target.
